file: 001 - Why Do POPULAR Girls Do This - 9.9M.mp4

voices.first_words: BRO, why are popular girls so annoying?
voices.sounds_like: ElevenLabs energetic young male TTS ('Liam'/'Josh' style), ~85% sure
voices.timing_notes: Shouts 'BRO' dry at 0:00.0, pauses 0.2s (0:00.5-0:00.7), fires staccato setup clauses (0:04.7, 0:05.6, 0:07.0) and fast jabs (0:09.7, 0:19.8), slows at 0:21.8-0:23.1 ('completely silent'), and sighs 'bro...' at 0:26.4.

Cuts in mid-sentence four times on all-caps punchlines—0:08.0-0:09.4 ('and they BOTH start LAUGHING'), 0:14.0-0:15.2 ('LAUGHING AGAIN'), 0:17.4-0:18.6 ('BRAD IS ASLEEP'), and 0:27.3-0:28.2 ('WE KNOW')—stretching vowels onto Vine booms.

voices.who: blonde popular girl in white crop top
voices.sounds_like: ElevenLabs/TikTok bratty teen female TTS ('Gigi'/'Bella' style), ~80% sure
voices.delivery: fake-annoyed on line 1; whiny compliment-fishing on line 2
voices.timing_notes: Snaps 'Brad, stop making me laugh!' briskly (0:16.0-0:16.9) before a 0.4s comedic pause (0:17.0-0:17.4); returns at 0:24.8-0:26.3 dragging out 'so bad' over the music-free room.

one_voice_plays_several_characters: no — three TTS voices: main narrator splits between a fast ~200 Hz teen male setup voice and a deep ~150 Hz ElevenLabs 'Adam' punchline baritone, plus a ~320 Hz teen female TTS for the popular girl.

music.description: quirky comedy-gaming loop with bouncy pizzicato strings, playful marimba plucks, light percussion
music.how_it_follows_the_story: Silent on 'BRO' (0:00.0-0:00.6), enters at 0:00.7 on the hook question, runs steadily under the hallway/whiteboard scenes, and cuts out at 0:21.7 on 'the class is completely silent' so crickets and the final joke land in dead air.

sound_effects.sound: exaggerated snoring groan and high whistle-snore
high-pitched cartoon cricket chirps and dry breeze
exasperated male vocal 'oh my god' groan

ambience: none during 0:00.0-0:21.7; sparse cartoon crickets in silent classroom (0:22.0-0:25.2)
sync_with_picture: 0:00.6 widen-cut sits in the post-'BRO' gap; 0:02.1 Vine boom hits her disgusted scowl and 0:02.6 boom hits the hallway cut; 0:06.1 groan matches her pink side-eye; 0:08.4 and 0:14.5 booms + giggles hit open-mouth pixel-tear laughs; 0:18.4 boom + 0:18.6 snore hit sleeping Brad's 'Z z' cut; music stops at 0:21.7 as a tumbleweed rolls (0:22.0); 0:27.7 boom hits 'WE KNOW'.
faces_and_mouths: Swapped 2D face decals on R6 heads rather than phoneme lip-sync: static smug/annoyed/puppy-eye decals snap on cuts, swapping to wide open-mouthed scream/laugh decals on bursts (0:08.4, 0:14.5, 0:17.4, 0:27.3).
comedic_or_emotional_timing: (1) Dry 'BRO' at 0:00.0 + 0.2s pause (0:00.5) before music; (2) mid-sentence baritone swap + Vine boom on 'BOTH start LAUGHING' (0:08.0) and 'LAUGHING AGAIN' (0:14.0); (3) 0.4s beat (0:17.0-0:17.4) before cutting to unconscious Brad snoring (0:18.6); (4) hard music kill at 0:21.7 for crickets before chopping 'WE KNOW' mid-boom at 0:28.2.
first_3_seconds: Loud dry male shout 'BRO!' at 0:00.0, a 0.2s gap (0:00.5-0:00.7), bouncy pizzicato/marimba BGM entering at 0:00.7 under 'why are popular girls so annoying?', and Vine booms at 0:02.1 and 0:02.6 — instant vocal urgency + meme bass impact.
ending: Hard smash-cut at 0:28.2 (-15.0 dB) mid-tail of 'WE KNOW!' and the 0:27.7 Vine boom; with music already muted since 0:21.7, it loops cleanly into the dry 0:00.0 'BRO!'.
mix: Loud, punchy (-13.1 LUFS, 0.2 dBTP, LRA 4.0 LU) with heavy sub-bass (48.1% <80 Hz from five 50 Hz Vine booms); dry crisp TTS voices in 250 Hz-4 kHz sit 12-15 dB above the clean BGM.
why_the_sound_works: Dry 'BRO!' at 0:00.0 + 0.2s gap creates high-contrast scroll-stopping urgency before music enters at 0:00.7.
Mid-sentence swaps to deep 'Adam' baritone + 50 Hz Vine booms (0:08.0, 0:14.0, 0:17.4, 0:27.3) turn complaints into audio punchlines.
Killing the BGM at 0:21.7 for quiet crickets makes the 'silent class' setup physically felt.
Cutting mid-decay on 'WE KNOW!' at 0:28.2 feeds straight back into 0:00.0 'BRO!' on replay.
unsure_about: Stock title of the 0:00.7-0:21.7 pizzicato/marimba loop (same track in 004, 007, 010, 016; left null).
